title: Finite subalgebra model of the closed-fibre section
statement: Let $A$ and $B$ be commutative rings, $I\subset A$ an ideal, and $B$ an étale $A$-algebra [def-weil-etale-morphism]. Given an $A$-algebra map $\sigma:B\to A/I$, there exist an $A$-subalgebra $D\subset B$ finite as an $A$-module [def-weil-finitely-generated-module], an $(A/I)$-algebra $C$, an isomorphism $\Phi:D/ID\cong A/I\times C$, and $b\in D$. The isomorphism respects the structure maps from $A/I$, sends the image of $b$ to $(1,0)$, and satisfies $\operatorname{pr}_1\Phi(\bar x)=\sigma(x)$ for every $x\in D$. The canonical map $D[1/b]\to B[1/b]$ [def-weil-ring-localization-away] is bijective. No Jacobson or root-lifting condition is assumed.

proof.text: Factor σ through B/IB. Étale quotient base change and the étale-section idempotent splitting give an A/I-algebra decomposition B/IB = A/I × C, with σ as first projection.

Étaleness gives finite presentation and hence finite type. Apply the integral-closure finite-fibre localization theorem to the finite first factor A/I. It supplies b in the integral closure, a compatible first-factor idempotent modulo I, and an isomorphism of its b-localization with B[1/b].

Write b²-b as a finite sum of I-coefficients times integral-closure elements. Choose finitely many numerators generating the integral-closure b-localization over A (B[1/b] is finite type). Let D be the A-subalgebra of B generated by b, the numerators, and the elements occurring in that sum. All generators are integral, so D is finite. Its b-localization injects into the integral-closure localization and surjects because its image contains the chosen generators and b⁻¹. Thus D[1/b] → B[1/b] is bijective.

The image of b in D/ID is idempotent. Localization commutes with quotient, so its first corner is A/I, identified by σ. Split off the complementary corner C, whose underlying type has the universe of B, and define Φ using this first-factor identification. The quotient structure map is inverse to the first-factor section, giving the asserted scalar formula and first projection.

lean.statement:
theorem exists_finite_gabber_section_model
    (A : Type u) [CommRing A] (I : Ideal A)
    (B : Type v) [CommRing B] [Algebra A B] [Etale A B]
    (σ : B →ₐ[A] A ⧸ I) :
    ∃ (D : Subalgebra A B) (_ : Module.Finite A D)
      (C : Type v) (_ : CommRing C) (_ : Algebra (A ⧸ I) C)
      (Φ : (D ⧸ I.map (algebraMap A D)) ≃+* ((A ⧸ I) × C)) (b : D),
      (∀ a : A, Φ (Ideal.Quotient.mk _ (algebraMap A D a)) =
        (algebraMap (A ⧸ I) (A ⧸ I) (Ideal.Quotient.mk I a),
          algebraMap (A ⧸ I) C (Ideal.Quotient.mk I a))) ∧
      Φ (Ideal.Quotient.mk _ b) = (1, 0) ∧
      (∀ x : D, (Φ (Ideal.Quotient.mk _ x)).1 = σ x.1) ∧
      Function.Bijective (Localization.awayMap D.val.toRingHom b)
